_provenance.limitation: an extent ending at the next entry is an upper bound when padding or data follows the body. 134 addresses in exe/fns.s are declared sections that fail the gate: handler blocks reached only through the table at D0x80010000, running on a register the dispatcher set and jumping to a shared epilogue, so they are blocks of a function rather than functions; those refused addresses are emitted per source under `rejected` so consumers can disposition them as blocks instead of unread functions. `jal <name>` calls to a named symbol are not counted as callers, because the caller regex reads an address and those lines carry none.
_provenance.method: entries come from four sources and extents run to the next entry: (1) the targets of `jal` instructions landing inside the same overlay, from the indexed assembly text; (2) a `.word` pointer target that opens a stack frame; (3) an address the shipped data segment declares a function pointer; (4) a symbol the assembly file itself declares as a `.section`+label pair, read from the file because the index drops directives. A source-4 entry whose name the extractor invented (`F0x…`) must also be called, open a frame, or return; a symbol carrying a real name is admitted on that alone. `j` and jump-table targets are deliberately NOT entries, because the card-effect dispatch blocks are branch targets inside one function and counting them would invent 348 functions.
